text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Franco-Egyptian summit will take place in Paris today to discuss ways to remove obstacles to peace. President Hosni Mubarak starts his visit to Washington tomorrow. He will meet President Bill Clinton, members of the administration and of Congress and businessmen. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said: "The Arabs will not pay the price for holding together the coalition government in Israel."
- Mubarak will meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat today before leaving for France. Arafat is on his way back from the United States.

- The cabinet has approved in principle the new trade law but the debate on details will continue into another session. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the law helps create a new climate in line with the realities of the age. It regulates commercial transactions in a way compatible with international changes and it conforms to Sharia, he added.

- The Ministry of Finance is preparing a new law on amicable settlements between the tax authorities and taxpayers. A source at the ministry said about 100,000 tax cases are now going through the legal system, with the state claiming about one billion pounds ($290 million).
- The cabinet extended the repayment period for popular housing to 40 years at five percent interest.

- Taher Helmi, a prominent lawyer and spokesman for the U.S.-Egyptian Presidents' Council, said in New York that the council had discussed the privatisation of 104 companies over two years. He said people are studying converting the national telecommunications organisation into a joint-stock company and selling its shares through the stock exchange. Other subjects under discussion are privatising one of the public-sector banks and amending the insurance law.

- An editorial by editor-in-chief Galal Duweidar says that after the talks betwen Mubarak and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu it was clear that Egypt said no to all Israeli positions which are hostile to peace and stability.

- Negotiations have started (in Europe) on the agricultural part of the association agreement with the European Union. Delegation member Saad Nassar said they would discuss Egyptian exports of fruits, vegetables and cotton.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid is now studying the memorandum from the Holding Company for Housing and Tourism on offering a tranche of shares in Cairo Housing and Development for sale to an anchor investor.
